mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of tightening.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real GDP signals a strengthening economy, which boosts corporate earnings and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of GDP growth.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3 percentage points within the last month signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage costs and reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of falling unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% within the last month signals increased economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and investor sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of increased industrial production.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts by more than 5% within the last two months signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of declining housing starts.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds the inflation rate (CPIAUCSL), it signals a real tightening of monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS exceeds CPIAUCSL.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points within the last month, it signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k & UNRATE decrease > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of strong payroll growth and falling unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real retail and food services sales (RSAFS) signals a strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and investor sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of increasing retail and food services sales.
